title: Network Failures, Timeouts, Retries, and Idempotency

scout.purpose: A resilient client distinguishes transport, protocol, parsing, authentication, rate-limit, and domain failures and retries only operations safe and useful to repeat.
scout.realWorldUse: Mobile networks disconnect, DNS fails, servers throttle, bodies corrupt, tokens expire, and users repeat actions while outcomes remain uncertain.
scout.outcome: Map typed failures, configure timeout layers, apply bounded backoff and jitter, preserve cancellation, and assess idempotency.

blocks.text: Transport failures include DNS, connection, TLS, socket, and offline errors and may surface as IOException. HTTP status is a completed exchange, not a transport exception. Deserialization and validation are representation failures. Authentication, authorization, conflict, rate limit, server failure, and domain rejection need distinct user and telemetry outcomes. Map client-specific exceptions to a sealed data failure at the source or repository boundary while preserving useful cause for diagnostics.

sections.title: Timeouts bound different phases and operations

blocks.text: OkHttp connect, read, write, and call timeouts bound transport phases differently. A coroutine timeout may bound the whole business operation including retries and parsing. Configure each from user experience and server behaviour, and document which fires first. Zero can mean no timeout and is rarely a safe production default. Cancellation should cancel the active call and backoff delay. Do not show offline solely from a connectivity callback; an attempted operation is the strongest evidence and local content should remain useful.

blocks.title: Retry is not error handling by repetition
blocks.text: It needs classification, repeatability, delay, budget, cancellation, and exhaustion.

sections.title: Retry is a constrained state machine

blocks.text: A retry state machine classifies failure, verifies operation repeatability, checks attempt and total time budgets, uses exponential backoff with jitter, honours Retry-After, and stops on cancellation. GET is commonly repeatable; POST requires a server idempotency contract. Retrying 401 without refreshing credentials loops pointlessly, and concurrent refresh needs single-flight coordination taught next week. Expose retrying and final failure as observable state and record attempts without sensitive data.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.text: Attempted operations and local-first behaviour remain the reliable product boundary.

inspect.title: Remove the retry-all loop
walkthrough: Throwable includes cancellation and serious failures, while createOrder may not be idempotent.
The loop has no attempt or total-time budget and fixed clients synchronize retries.
Classify transport failure, require idempotency, cap attempts, jitter backoff, and expose exhaustion.
inspect.expectedOutput: One logical order has a bounded observable outcome and cancellation stops immediately.

trap_check.mistake: Mapping every failure to No internet.
trap_check.why: Authentication, parsing, conflict, and server failures require different recovery.
trap_check.fix: Use typed data failures and user outcomes.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Build a cancellable retry engine with typed transport and HTTP failures, timeout budget, exponential backoff and jitter, Retry-After support, and idempotency gating.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Permanent and authentication failures do not loop. Cancellation stops active call or delay. Virtual-time tests prove attempts, delays, and exhaustion.

recall.prompt: Is an HTTP 500 a transport exception?
recall.answer: No, it is a completed HTTP response with failure status.
Many clients retrying in synchronized waves.

recall.prompt: What must cancellation do during retry delay?
recall.answer: Stop the retry state machine immediately.
